name: Slack

auth.keyHelp: Create your own Slack app, add only the read scopes (channels:read, groups:read, channels:history, groups:history, users:read), install it to the workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token.

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: Slack returns HTTP 200 for failures too: every response is JSON with ok true or false and an error code (invalid_auth, not_authed, ...), so the host must check ok, not the status. Bot tokens start with xoxb-; send them as 'Authorization: Bearer xoxb-...' and use 'Content-type: application/json' on JSON POSTs (the token must be in the header, not the JSON body). auth.test needs no scopes and returns url, team, user, team_id, user_id, bot_id. Scopes per method: conversations.list needs channels:read, groups:read, im:read, mpim:read (page does not say whether all or any one is needed); conversations.history needs the matching *:history scope; users.list needs users:read; chat.postMessage needs chat:write, and a new app can only post to channels the bot has joined unless chat:write.public is added. A read-only key is possible by installing the app with only read scopes. The method pages do not describe how the bearer header is used on the token-type page, which is why the header format comes from the Web API overview. The official Slack MCP server (https://mcp.slack.com/mcp) is NOT usable with a plain bot token: it needs a directory-published or internal Slack app using confidential OAuth with user tokens (client_id and client_secret; no Dynamic Client Registration, no SSE); unlisted apps are prohibited and workspace admins approve it.
